hints.title: Difference of Upper Bounds
hints.text: Counting contiguous segments with an exact count of distinct items directly is tricky. Express the exact count as the difference between counting segments with at most k distinct items and segments with at most k - 1 distinct items.

hints.title: Monotonic Window Contraction
hints.text: For at most distinct items, expand the right endpoint and record item frequencies. When the number of unique items exceeds the bound, advance the left endpoint until the count fits again.

hints.title: Window Length Accumulation
hints.text: For each valid right index, the number of valid ending subarrays is right - left + 1. Sum these counts across all right indices for atMost(k) and subtract atMost(k - 1) to produce the exact answer.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all O(N^2) subarrays and checking distinct counts takes O(N^2) time, which times out for large N.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking element frequencies in a sliding window trades O(N) extra space for linear time complexity.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the exact(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1) decomposition for sliding windows.
complexity.notes: Frequency table size is bounded by distinct elements within the current window.
